title: Your First Swap on an AMM
objectives: Execute a decentralized token swap on our course AMM
Inspect trade quotes, exchange rates, and slippage tolerances
Understand why the price shifts slightly after every trade

steps.title: Trading Without a Middleman
steps.body:
In traditional finance, trading stocks requires a broker, a clearing house, and bank business hours. In DeFi, a <Term id="swap">swap</Term> happens directly against an on-chain smart contract in under 1 second, 24/7, from anyone on earth.

When you request a <Term id="quote">quote</Term>, the <Term id="amm">AMM</Term> computes three things before you commit:
1. The current spot exchange rate between the two pool reserves
2. The expected output amount based on the pool formula
3. The estimated <Term id="price_impact">price impact</Term> of your order size

**Why the quote is not a promise.** The number you see is based on the pool's state *right now*. Between the moment you click and the moment your transaction lands, other traders can move the price. That is exactly why the next step - slippage - exists. Reading the quote carefully is how you avoid paying far more than you intended.

steps.title: Slippage Tolerance: Your Safety Buffer
steps.body:
Because multiple people trade on the blockchain at the same time, the pool price might move while your transaction is travelling to the validator. Without protection, you could receive noticeably less than your quote promised.

Your <Term id="slippage">slippage tolerance</Term> (e.g. 0.5% or 1%) tells the contract: *'If the market moves against me and I would receive less than my minimum guaranteed amount, abort the transaction and refund my tokens.'*

**Choosing the right number.** Set it too tight on a volatile token and your swap fails repeatedly; set it too loose and you expose yourself to <Term id="sandwich_attack">sandwich attacks</Term> and terrible fills. For liquid pairs, ~0.5% is usually a healthy default. The tolerance is a safety buffer, not a target.

steps.title: Under the Hood: The Swap Instruction
steps.body: When executing a swap instruction on our Anchor AMM, the program receives: `amount_in` and `min_out`. It calculates `amount_out` using the vault reserves and fee rate. Before transferring tokens, it asserts `amount_out >= min_out`. If the condition fails, the instruction reverts with an error code, protecting you from front-running or wild price swings.

questions.prompt: What does a 1% slippage tolerance setting guarantee?
options: You are guaranteed to make a 1% profit on the trade
The trade will only execute if you receive at least 99% of your quoted output; otherwise it safely cancels
You pay 1% in extra gas fees to validators
Your trade executes instantly with no checks
questions.explainRight: Correct! Slippage tolerance sets the minimum output floor you are willing to accept.
questions.explainWrong: Incorrect. Slippage tolerance protects you by cancelling the trade if the price moved worse than your set threshold.

questions.prompt: Why does a token's price increase inside an AMM pool when someone buys it?
options: The developers manually adjust the price
The buyer deposited payment tokens and removed target tokens, making the target token scarcer in the pool
It is determined by the central bank
questions.explainRight: Spot on! Constant product math ensures that as reserve X shrinks, each remaining unit of X costs more units of Y.
questions.explainWrong: Incorrect. Buying a token removes it from the pool, making it scarcer and driving up its relative cost.
